propositions: Phase 2 removed 827 truncated bridge-echo duplicate comments across three Jira issues (REB-2605, REB-1931, REB-1567) that lacked the reconciler marker because truncation appended the marker after the body, cutting it off.

Comments qualified for deletion only if they contained the reconciler's truncation suffix AND lacked the RECONCILER_MARKER, identifying them as reconciler-generated duplicates rather than foreign comments.
For each distinct normalized comment body, the oldest copy (lowest comment id) was retained and all others deleted, with zero data loss verified by post-deletion re-fetch reconciliation.

The bridge will re-post approximately one copy per distinct truncated comment on its first pass after re-enablement because comment_ids map remains empty until new posts are recorded, but this is expected and handled by subsequent deduplication passes.

The keep-one rule must invert for the final post-re-enable sweep: retain the copy whose id appears in the recorded comment_ids map rather than the oldest, because the bridge records only newly posted ids and keeping the oldest would orphan the map and recreate the original defect.
